apps.name: DroneDeploy Flight App
apps.releaseNotes:
New Features

  - RTK connect in flight — Drones can now connect to RTK mid-flight by pausing at the first waypoint, suspending, then resuming
  - Starting waypoint offset slider — New planning UI control to calibrate the starting waypoint position on long flight legs
  - Terrain Awareness — Expanded acreage limit for terrain awareness missions
  - Flight log timestamps — Timestamps now shown alongside entries in the timeline viewer

  Improvements

  - Firmware alerts — Only flags firmware that is genuinely older than required, reducing false update prompts
  - Camera display names — All supported cameras now show human-readable names throughout the app
  - Travel altitude — Resets automatically when switching back to automatic altitude settings
  - RTK stability — Consolidated connection paths and prompts drone reset when RTK datum changes mid-connection
  - Mission reliability — Flight path changes are now applied synchronously; numeric values in mission JSON rounded to prevent floating-point drift

  Bug Fixes

  - App startup & navigation — Fixed 60-second startup delay on legacy-auth devices and unsigned sessions; fixed invisible text on the active mobile
  nav tab
  - Missions & planning — Fixed geofence RTH marked as failed when all waypoints completed; fixed image count using stale data after flight path
  changes; fixed non-resumable missions appearing in the queue; fixed approach waypoint heading
  - Capture — Fixed pano missions capturing half the expected photos on thermal drones; fixed Progress Video recording before the gimbal reached its
  planned angle
  - Stand assessment — Fixed markers not loading, gimbal angle on first photo, and PDF reports downloading as 0 bytes
  - Map & visualization — Fixed FPV view maximizing to map instead of camera from vertical layout; fixed wrong direction in aircraft detection
  messages

apps.releaseNotes:
NAVAL UPDATE

PLAYER MADE BOATS

Player-made boats are here, providing a new way to explore the seas, including the Deep Sea!

Place the new Boat Building Station deployable in the water and get building with your shipmates! Use the new Boat Building Plan to construct your dream boat, utilising a new set of boat-specific building blocks.

Add a steering wheel, anchor, sails, engines, planks, ramps and cannons to complete your vessel and head off into the Deep Sea!

Careful consideration and placement of your engines and sails is important if you want a seaworthy ship, as they will affect its handling and speed. Sails and engines can both be reversed using the radial menu options for some nifty reverse parking.

Be sure to set a lock code on your steering wheel to stop unwanted access or theft of your shiny new boat.

Regular deployables can be placed on your boats. If they work on the Tugboat, they'll work here too.

Need to make a change after realising your boat just goes in circles? Use the Deploy & Edit mode (not available in the Deep Sea) to quickly and easily deploy a Boat Building Station around your boat.

Have fun building and exploring the seas!

NEW BOAT DEPLOYABLES

To get your vessel sea worthy, we've now got some new deployables - specifically for your boat!

Boat Building Station

The boat-building station is placeable in deep water, it's used to build and edit your boat.

Building plan

The boat-building plan is similar to the building planner you know and love, but for boats.

Sails

A sheet of toughened fabric rigged to catch the wind and help propel the boat forwards.

Helm

A must-have for any seaworthy boat. Used to steer and control your direction, with a built-in lock to keep your vessel secure when you’re not at the wheel.

Engine

A powerful motor that runs on low grade fuel and burns through it fast. Loud, thirsty, and inefficient, but invaluable when you need to escape danger, chase down other players, or muscle your way out of a bad situation. Sometimes speed is worth the cost.

Anchor

A heavy anchor used to stop your boat drifting. Drop it to hold position and keep your vessel exactly where you want it. Without it, your boat may drift to shore. 

Canon

A powerful naval weapon used to sink other players’ boats. Load it with cannon balls.

Small Ramp

Bridge gaps and create quick access points. Ideal for boarding other ships or reaching land from the water.

Plank

Used to bridge gaps, board other boats, and settle minor disagreements by pushing friends into open water.

THE DEEP SEA

The Deep Sea is a new offshore region you can travel to using boats. It’s high risk, high reward, and intentionally unforgiving.

You can access it by sailing toward the edge of the map using a strong boat such as player-made boats, RHIBs or the new PT boats.

This is not a place to live: you cannot build, and nothing respawns. First come, first served. The deep sea will open and close intermittently, like a world event.

Inside, you can explore new content detailed below in this blog:

•
Tropical islands
[/*]
•
Floating cities
[/*]
•
Ghost ships
[/*]
•
Boats controlled by scientists
[/*]

We have lots of plans to expand deep-sea and use it as a bridge between worlds.

GHOST SHIPS

Similar to monuments, Ghost Ships are stationary ships scattered throughout the deep sea and filled with loot for people to scavenge while navigating on their boats.

Each Ghost Ship is protected by scientists, both on the ship and nearby patrols who will try to keep you off the ship. Some Ghost Ships also contain locked crates, which you'll need to hack while being under pressure of other players and scientist boats.

We hope that Ghost Ships, along with other loot locations such as tropical islands provide enough incentive to visit the deep sea often. 

DEEP SEA FLOATING CITIES

apps.name: Tor Browser
apps.releaseNotes:
Tor Browser 16.0 is now available for Desktop and Android. This is our first stable release based on Firefox ESR 153, incorporating a year's worth of changes that have been shipped upstream in Firefox. As part of this process, we've also completed our annual ESR transition audit, where we reviewed and addressed over 270 Bugzilla issues covering changes in Firefox that could negatively affect the privacy and security of Tor Browser users.

What's new for Desktop?

Redesigned Settings
Tor Browser connects millions of people to the Tor network (and by extension, the free and open internet) out of the box. However, for those who need to circumvent advanced censorship, boost their security level, or tailor their browsing experience, clear and easy-to-use Settings are essential. To that end, Tor Browser 16.0 introduces a complete redesign of the Settings experience based on a parallel redesign shipped in Firefox in June. Improvements include a cleaner layout, updated navigation, and clearer labels and descriptions aimed at making settings easier to find, understand, and manage. Other noteworthy changes include:
- The long-standing "General" page has been retired, with its contents distributed across new pages for Appearance, Downloads, Tabs and browsing, Accessibility and Languages.
- Pages and components that are unique to Tor browser like Connection and Security Level have been rebuilt from scratch using Firefox's new components so they look and feel consistent with the rest of Settings.
- Some settings that, if enabled, could compromise your privacy or make your browser easier to fingerprint have either been hidden or feature clear warnings.
Fear not: your existing preferences will remain saved even if the original setting has moved or changed, and you can use the search bar at the top of Settings to find anything you're struggling to track down.

Generic window titles
Another new addition to Settings is the option to use generic window titles, which can be found under Privacy and security → Protections from third‑party applications. Like most browsers, Tor Browser uses the title of the page you're currently viewing for the names of its windows. However, other applications on your computer or your operating system itself can read these titles without special permissions. When enabled, this option simply replaces all window titles with "Tor Browser" — preventing other software from snooping on your browsing history. As always, for more comprehensive protection from third‑party applications on your device, we recommend using Tails.
For now, this option is strictly opt‑in, as we did not have sufficient time during this release cycle to properly evaluate potential side‑effects for users. In particular, we worry that enabling this setting may reduce the browser's usability for those who rely on accessibility tools (e.g. screen‑readers) or those with highly customized systems (e.g. less‑popular desktop managers, application switchers, etc). If you are one of these users, we would ask that you try using this setting, and report back any bugs or usability issues you find!
📣 Generic window titles have also been upstreamed to Firefox as part of the Tor Uplift Project. Advanced Firefox users can enable this feature by opening about:config and setting privacy.exposeContentTitleInWindow (for normal windows) and privacy.exposeContentTitleInWindow.pbm (for private browsing windows) to false.

New user manual
The Tor Browser manual, which can be found by visiting about:manual or through the application menu (☰) → Help → Tor Browser manual, has also received a complete revamp. Since the release of our new Support portal in 2025, the team has had to maintain two sets of documentation: one for the traditional manual that's available to read in Tor Browser, and another for the new Support site. With this release, we've solved that problem by replacing the older material in the Tor Browser manual with our latest and greatest help content from the ne…
